applied. ``since_unix_nano`` is inclusive, ``until_unix_nano``
exclusive, both against ``received_at_unix_nano`` (not span start).

built from the last row of this one as
``"<received_at_unix_nano>:<span_id>"`` — for example
``"1700000000000000000:9f2c1a"``. A malformed cursor is an error;
it never silently restarts at page one. Rows ingested after a page
was served are newer than that page's cursor and will appear in a
later call, not a repeated one.

tools.description:

and how slow the slow tail was.

``selector`` and ``task_class`` are matched with NULL-aware equality,
so passing ``None`` selects the rows where that column IS NULL rather
than dropping them. Half-NULL pairs are the common case, and treating
NULL as "no match" would under-report them as healthy zeros.

Only ``success`` and ``error`` spans are scored — a span still in
flight when it landed is neither, and counting it would pad the
failure-rate denominator. The p99 is computed over the scored spans
that carry a latency, so it is a different population from
``span_count``.

workflow, then binds the resulting ``workflow_id`` to the task
through session-buddy's ``tasks_link_workflow``. The workflow
runs FIRE-AND-FORGET, so the task is bound to a workflow that is
still running; a failure between steps 2 and 3 emits
``task.handoff_orphan`` so the sweeper can re-link later.

The dispatch is scoped to ONE repository. Without an explicit
scope the durable path fans out over the whole repository
catalog, which for a single task is a fleet-wide run — so the
scope comes from ``params.repo`` or the task's
``metadata["repo"]``, and a task with neither is refused.

Rate limit: 10 calls/minute per caller.

Spawn a durable worker AND register a settle record BEFORE any file write.

a process crash cannot leave a worker writing files without an
audit trail. The returned ``run_ref`` is the durable handle for
subsequent :func:`mahavishnu_worker_settle` calls.

The ``bindings`` payload is a JSON-friendly list of ``{"path": str,
"base": str}`` dicts — ``path`` is the binding's location relative
to the worker repo, ``base`` is the pre-run content snapshot used
for the 3-way merge during ``apply``.

tools.description:
Drive a settle run through its lifecycle.

``action`` is one of ``select | apply | release | discard``. The
state machine (:mod:`mahavishnu.settle.state_machine`) enforces
legal transitions and raises :class:`SettleTransitionError` for
illegal ones.

For ``apply``, callers must pass ``bindings_content`` — a mapping of
``path -> ours`` (the worker's candidate content for each binding).
Each binding is 3-way merged with ``git merge-file`` against the
base snapshot captured at ``mahavishnu_worker_run_with_settle`` time. Conflicts
surface as a structured :class:`MergeConflictError` payload (the
merged-with-markers text is returned so the caller can decide how
to proceed).

``bindings_theirs`` is an optional mapping of ``path -> theirs`` for
the 3-way merge. When omitted, ``theirs`` defaults to the binding's
``base`` (the "first apply" case — ours is adopted cleanly when it
differs from base in non-overlapping ways).

tools.description:
Query the local record store for a task class.

Session-Buddy has no local OpenTelemetry span store -- it emits spans
to the fleet collector and reads its own records back from the
reflection database. This tool queries those local records through the
fleet-wide `query_local_traces` envelope:

* `task_class` matches the record's classification (`category` or
  `subcategory`). The values present are memory categories such as
  "facts" and "context" -- NOT the OpenTelemetry task taxonomy
  ("code", "code_generation", "mcp_tool_call"), which this store
  does not carry. A `task_class` from the OTel taxonomy matches
  nothing here, and that is an accurate answer: this server has no
  traces for it.
* `system_id` matches the record's `project` -- the basename of the
  directory the writing session ran in. In a plain checkout that is
  the repo name ("mahavishnu"); in a worktree checkout it is the
  worktree directory name, so a filter for the repo name will not
  find records written from a worktree. The match is exact (case
  insensitive). A record written by a consolidated multi-project
  session carries a comma-joined list and is not reachable by any
  single-project filter. A record with no project is excluded by a
  project filter.

This reads conversation and checkpoint rows (``conversations_v2``).
Reflections written via `store_reflection` live in a different table
and are NOT returned -- use `quick_search` or `search_conversations`
for those.

The window bounds are absolute ISO8601 timestamps. A bound with no
offset is read as UTC. A bound that does not parse is rejected: the
call returns an empty list rather than running an unbounded query.

Returns a list of records; an empty list means no record matched the
filter, or the store was unreachable, so an empty result does not
distinguish "no matches" from "query failed". Set `dry_run` to get the
stored metadata instead of the record body; that mode clamps `limit`
to 20 and keeps your `system_id` and `task_class` filters in force.
Side effect: none; reads the record store only.
tools.name: query_local_traces

tools.description:
Bind a task to the workflow it was dispatched to. Link-once.

The only writer of ``Task.workflow_id``. The caller-supplied
``metadata`` bag on ``tasks_update`` cannot reach the field — server-set
fields are never sourced from a caller-supplied container.

Link-once semantics (contract C3): a task binds to exactly one
workflow. Re-linking to the SAME id is an idempotent no-op that returns
the task unchanged (the orphan sweeper retries a link after a step-3
failure, and a retry must not be an error); re-linking to a DIFFERENT
id is refused with ``workflow_already_linked``.

Returns the updated :class:`Task``, or an error envelope on rate
limit / pattern mismatch / not_found / not_visible / already linked.
tools.name: session_buddy_tasks_link_workflow
